newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch closing debt market report.
newsitem.headline: Dutch closing debt market report.

text.p: Dutch bonds closed weaker on Tuesday but near their day's highs after a late spike, as U.S. military and economic developments held world attention.

Dealers said a lower than expected rise in the U.S. National Association of Purchasing Management's (NAPM) index of manufacturing activity in August boosted major world bond markets, taking guilder state loans with them.
"It wasn't as bad as a lot of people expected. The U.S. market bounced. We merely followed," said one dealer.
The market had earlier weakened through the day on news of U.S. military strikes on targets in Iraq.
Another factor was a Wall Street Journal report that U.S. interest rates would rise by a sharper than expected 50 basis points if signs did not emerge of slowing economic activity.
"(The NAPM index) at least indicates that inflation isn't running as high as expected," said another dealer.
But a trader said market participants were waiting for more U.S. data this week, with August payroll figures out on Friday.
"There's no clear picture out there," he said.
He also reported switching between maturities in the middle of the guilder yield curve but little overall volume.
